course_used.anna: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE25302); also Circuits and Network Analysis (EC25C02)

subtopics.t: Relationships and conversions between parameter sets
Interconnection of two-ports: series, parallel and cascade
Network synthesis: RC and LC functions, Foster and Cauer

where.title: Resonance and Two Port Networks
topics: Resonant circuits: series, parallel, series-parallel circuits
effect of variation of Q on resonance
Relations between circuit parameters: Q, resonant frequency and bandwidth
Two Port Networks, terminal pairs, relationship of two port variables
impedance parameters, admittance parameters, transmission parameters and hybrid parameters
Balanced Three-Phase Voltages: Wye-Wye, Wye- Delta, Delta-Delta Connections
Three-Phase Power Measurement using two wattmeter method.
Concept of one port, two-port and multi-port networks
Behavior of elements with ac signals
Generalization of Network Theorems and Circuit Analysis
Transient and Steady-state Response of Circuits
Laplace Transformation and its application to circuit analysis
Network Functions (Driving point impedance and admittance)

where.title: Two Port Networks
topics: Two port networks-characterization in terms of impedance
output impedance and gain of terminated two-ports in terms of two-port parameters and termination impedance
Applications of two-port parameters in negative feedback systems
power transmission Dependent source equivalent circuits for coupled coils
ac steady-state analysis of circuits containing coupled coils
the perfectly coupled two-winding transformer and the ideal two-winding transformer

where.title: Total Number of contact hours
topics: Initial and final conditions in RL
RC and RLC Circuits for DC Excitations
General and Particular solution of the first order and second order circuits
Applications of Laplace transform in finding solution or RC
Response of RC circuits for step
Two port network- Open circuit impedance parameters

other_units.name: Foundations: Circuit Elements and Laws
subtopics: Circuit elements R, L, C and their V-I relations
Independent and dependent voltage and current sources
Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's laws
Network terminology: node, branch, loop, mesh
Series-parallel circuits; voltage and current division
Star-delta transformation
Source transformation
Network topology: graphs, tie-sets and cut-sets

other_units.name: Mesh, Nodal Analysis and Network Theorems
subtopics: Mesh analysis and supermesh
Nodal analysis and supernode
Linearity and superposition theorem
Thevenin's and Norton's theorems
Maximum power transfer theorem
Reciprocity, Millman's and Tellegen's theorems
Compensation theorem
Applying network theorems to AC circuits

other_units.name: Sinusoidal Steady State and AC Power
subtopics: Sinusoids: RMS and average values, form factor
Phasors and phasor diagrams
Impedance and admittance
Steady-state analysis of RL, RC and RLC circuits
Real, reactive, apparent and complex power; power factor
Balanced and unbalanced three-phase circuits
Three-phase power measurement: two-wattmeter method
Non-sinusoidal waveforms: Fourier series, RMS value, THD

other_units.name: Resonance and Coupled Circuits
subtopics: Series resonance
Parallel resonance
Quality factor, bandwidth and selectivity
Frequency response of RC and RLC circuits
Locus diagrams of RL, RC and RLC circuits
Self and mutual inductance; coefficient of coupling
Dot convention and analysis of coupled coils
Ideal and linear transformers
Magnetic circuits: MMF, flux and reluctance

other_units.name: Transient Analysis and Laplace Transform
subtopics: Initial and final conditions in RL, RC, RLC circuits
Source-free RL and RC circuits; time constant
Step response of first-order circuits; natural and forced response
Second-order RLC circuits: overdamped, critically damped, underdamped
Natural frequency and damping ratio
Transient response with sinusoidal excitation
Laplace transform and s-domain circuit analysis
Network functions, transfer functions, poles and zeros
State-variable analysis of circuits
